Overview

The BUILDVERSE Hackathon brings together developers, students, innovators, and technology enthusiasts to build real-world solutions across AI, education, healthcare, fintech, sustainability, social impact, and open innovation.

Participants can build from anywhere, collaborate with fellow innovators, and turn their ideas into working solutions that can be showcased on stage.

MEET THE ORGANIZERS

WHY PARTICIPATE?

  • Explore 6 diverse tracks across technology and social impact.
  • Build and collaborate with fellow developers and innovators.
  • Work on real-world problems using the technologies you choose.
  • Get an opportunity to showcase your solution on stage.
  • Win prizes, swag, and certificates.
  • Connect with the wider technology and innovation community.

HACKATHON EXPERIENCE

Build your solution over 2 days, collaborate with your team, and bring your best ideas to life. Whether you're working on AI, FinTech, HealthTech, EdTech, Sustainability, Social Impact, or an open innovation idea, BUILDVERSE gives you the freedom to create and experiment.

Innovate. Collaborate. Create Impact.

Build Trustworthy and Resilient AI Agents with DeepAgentLabs

AI agents are increasingly capable of reasoning, using tools, calling APIs, and taking autonomous actions. As these systems become more capable, understanding their behavior and ensuring they remain reliable when things go wrong becomes increasingly important. Your challenge is to build an innovative AI agent or agentic application using AgenticLens, Agentic-Chaos, or both from the DeepAgentLabs open-source ecosystem . Use AgenticLens to bring observability into your agent by capturing and analyzing areas such as workflows, tool calls, traces, latency, cost, evaluations, and failures. Use Agentic-Chaos to test the resilience of your agent by introducing controlled failures into models, tools, APIs, or other dependencies and analyzing how the system responds and recovers. Choose any real-world use case and demonstrate how observability, resilience testing, or a combination of both can help build more reliable and trustworthy AI agents. Build it. Observe it. Break it safely. Make it resilient.

Responsible AI & Inclusive InnovationRead more

AI for Accessibility & Inclusion

Use AI and emerging technologies to remove barriers for people with disabilities and make digital and physical experiences more inclusive.

Responsible AI & Inclusive InnovationRead more

AI Evals & Judging AI

Build innovative ways to evaluate, benchmark, judge, or audit AI systems and agents . Projects can explore automated evaluators, LLM-as-a-judge, agent evaluations, hallucination detection, bias testing, safety benchmarks, or human-vs-AI evaluation frameworks.

Eligibility

Profile Type:
Students
  • The hackathon is open to students, developers, innovators, and technology enthusiasts.
  • Participants can register as individuals or form a team of 2–4 members.
  • All team members must complete their registration on the Buildora platform.
  • Participants can build solutions across any of the listed themes and tracks.
  • Teams are encouraged to create original, meaningful solutions addressing real-world problems.

Rules

1. Eligibility

  • The hackathon is open to participants who meet the eligibility criteria mentioned on the event page.
  • Participants must provide accurate information during registration.
  • Participants must complete registration before the stated deadline.

2. Team Formation

  • Participants can participate subject to the team-size limit specified on the event page.
  • All team members must be registered on the hackathon platform.
  • Each participant can be part of only one team.
  • Team changes after the submission deadline may not be permitted.

3. Project Requirements

  • Projects must address a meaningful problem and align with at least one of the listed themes.
  • Participants are encouraged to build functional prototypes or working solutions.
  • Submissions must be original work created by the participating team.
  • Existing projects may be used as a foundation only if the team makes meaningful contributions during the hackathon.

4. Technology & AI Tools

  • Participants are free to use programming languages, frameworks, APIs, SDKs, open-source libraries, cloud services, and AI tools.
  • Generative AI, AI agents, APIs, and third-party tools are permitted.
  • Participants are responsible for complying with the terms and licenses of any third-party technology they use.
  • Any significant use of third-party components should be disclosed where requested in the submission.

5. Submission

Each submission should include the information requested on the platform, which may include:

  • Problem statement
  • Solution description
  • Key features
  • Technology stack
  • Demo or prototype
  • Repository or relevant links
  • Demo video, if required

All submissions must be completed before the stated deadline.

6. Judging Criteria

Projects may be evaluated based on:

  • Innovation — Originality and creativity of the idea.
  • Problem Relevance — How effectively the solution addresses the chosen problem.
  • Technical Execution — Quality and effectiveness of the implementation.
  • Impact — Potential real-world value and scalability.
  • User Experience — Usability, accessibility, and overall experience.
  • Presentation — Clarity of the submission and demonstration.

7. Intellectual Property

  • Participants must have the necessary rights to use all code, content, datasets, APIs, models, images, and other assets included in their submission.
  • Plagiarism, unauthorized copying, or intellectual property infringement is not permitted.
  • Participants retain ownership of their original work unless otherwise stated in the specific hackathon terms.

8. Prohibited Content

Submissions must not contain content that is illegal, harmful, abusive, discriminatory, defamatory, or that violates the rights of others.

9. Disqualification

A submission may be disqualified if:

  • It violates the hackathon rules.
  • It contains plagiarized or fraudulent work.
  • False information is provided.
  • The submission is made after the deadline without an approved extension.
  • The project infringes third-party intellectual property.
  • The team attempts to manipulate the judging or submission process.

The organizers reserve the right to disqualify submissions that do not comply with the rules.

10. Final Decision

The organizers' decisions regarding eligibility, judging, and disqualification will be final.
